item.title: Xi calls for carrying forward Sun Yat-sen's legacy in national rejuvenation drive
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-12
Chinese President Xi Jinping, also general secretary of the Communist Party of China Central Committee and chairman of the Central Military Commission, addresses a gathering to commemorate the 160th anniversary of Sun Yat-sen's birth at the Great Hall of the People in Beijing, capital of China, Nov. 12, 2026. (Xinhua/Yue Yuewei) BEIJING, Nov. 12 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping on Thursday called for carrying forward the legacy of Sun Yat-sen, one of the nation's revered revolutionary forefathers, to make joint efforts for national rejuvenation and turn into reality the great dream of all Chinese people since the advent of modern times. Xi, also general secretary of the Communist Party of China (CPC) Central Committee and chairman of the Central Military Commission, made the remarks at a gathering held in Beijing to commemorate the 160th anniversary of Sun's birth. Born in 1866, Sun led the Revolution of 1911 more than a century ago to abolish the absolute monarchy that had ruled China for thousands of years. Sun died in 1925. Thursday's gathering in the Great Hall of the People was attended by about 3,000 people, including senior Chinese leaders Li Qiang, Zhao Leji, Wang Huning, Cai Qi, Ding Xuexiang and Li Xi, who are members of the Standing Committee of the Political Bureau of the CPC Central Committee. Wang presided over the event. Xi met with Sun's relatives and representatives of overseas guests before the event started. In his speech, Xi hailed Sun as a great national hero, a great patriot and a great pioneer of China's democratic revolution. He said that Chinese communists are the most steadfast supporters, loyal collaborators, and faithful successors to the revolutionary cause initiated by Sun. For more than 100 years, the CPC has led the Chinese people in writing the most magnificent chapter in the history of the Chinese nation, Xi said. "The best way for us to remember Dr. Sun is to emulate, inherit and carry forward his invaluable spirit, steadily advancing our endeavors to build a great country and rejuvenate our nation," Xi said. Highlighting Sun's lifelong devotion to the country, Xi called on all Chinese people to learn from Sun and promote patriotism to strive for a strong and prosperous China. He also lauded Sun's dedication to the people, underscoring the imperative of always putting the people first and serving them wholeheartedly. On the new journey, it is essential to make solid headway in promoting well-rounded personal development and common prosperity for all, Xi stressed. Noting that Sun devoted his life to the pursuit of truth, Xi stressed the need to learn from Sun's example, advance theoretical exploration and innovation with courage, and continue to write new chapters in adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of the times. Xi called on the Chinese people to carry forward Sun's unyielding determination, rise to challenges ahead and break new ground in the country's development. "We must carry forward the fighting spirit, build up our ability, be ready to withstand high winds, choppy waters, and even dangerous storms, and overcome all the risks and challenges we face on the way forward," Xi said. Calling on people to learn from Sun's commitment to unity, Xi also emphasized adhering to the united front and strengthening the great unity among all the sons and daughters of the Chinese nation. Highlighting Sun's global vision, Xi called for vigorously promoting the common values of humanity and actively advancing the building of a community with a shared future for humanity. "Dr. Sun always upheld national unity and ethnic solidarity, and resolutely opposed any word or act attempting to split the country and divide the nation," Xi said. Resolving the Taiwan question and realizing the complete reunification of the motherland is an unwavering historical mission for the CPC, the shared aspiration of all Chinese people, and a natural requirement for the great rejuvenation of the Chinese nation, Xi stressed. People on both sides of the Taiwan Strait and all Chinese at home and abroad should join hands to oppose the "Taiwan independence" secessionist forces, and work together for the peaceful development of cross-Strait relations and the complete reunification of the motherland, Xi said. "On the basis of adhering to the one-China principle and the 1992 Consensus, we are willing to engage in dialogue and consultations with people of vision and insight from all sectors in Taiwan on matters related to cross-Strait relations and national reunification," Xi said. "We will definitely give full consideration to Taiwan's realities and take full account of the interests and feelings of our compatriots in Taiwan," Xi said. "But we will never leave any room for 'Taiwan independence' separatist activities in any form." "The historical trends are unstoppable. The complete reunification of our motherland must be realized, and it can, without doubt, be realized," Xi said. A gathering commemorating the 160th anniversary of Sun Yat-sen's birth is held at the Great Hall of the People in Beijing, capital of China, Nov. 12, 2026. Xi Jinping, Li Qiang, Zhao Leji, Wang Huning, Cai Qi, Ding Xuexiang and Li Xi attended the gathering here on Thursday. (Xinhua/Yao Dawei)

item.title: Accepting Tokyo Trials' verdicts, a prerequisite for Japan's return to the international community after World War II
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-12
Chinese foreign ministry spokesperson Mao Ning When asked to comment on the 78th anniversary of the verdict delivered by the International Military Tribunal for the Far East, or the Tokyo Trials, Chinese foreign ministry spokesperson Mao Ning said on Thursday that history must never be forgotten, and justice must never be challenged. The international community should work together to oppose all attempts to whitewash the history of aggression and revive militarism. Mao said that on this day 78 years ago, following two and a half years of proceedings, the Tokyo Trials, based on overwhelming evidence and rigorous legal reasoning, found that Japanese militarism had waged wars of aggression and committed serious violations of international law, sentencing 25 Class-A Japanese war criminals. The verdict exposed Japan's wartime atrocities to the world and left an enduring mark of historical disgrace. The Tokyo Trials are an integral part of the postwar international order, and accepting their verdicts was a prerequisite for Japan's return to the international community after World War II. For years, Japanese right-wing forces have disregarded the historical conclusions of the Tokyo Trials, vigorously denied or even glorified the country's crimes of aggression, and promoted a distorted view of history, a stance that is deeply deplorable, Mao said. According to Mao, what is particularly alarming is that in recent years, the Japanese government has accelerated its remilitarization by sharply increasing defense spending, expanding offensive military capabilities, seeking revisions to the three security documents and moving to abandon its Three Non-Nuclear Principles. These moves will seriously challenge the fundamental legal principles established by the Tokyo Trials and pose a grave threat to regional peace and stability, Mao said. History must never be forgotten, and justice must never be challenged. The international community should work together to oppose all attempts to whitewash the history of aggression and revive militarism, Mao said. China stands ready to join peace-loving countries and peoples around the world in firmly upholding historical truth, safeguarding the postwar international order, and defending international fairness and justice, Mao said.

item.title: Chinese Peacekeepers to Lebanon Conduct Humanitarian Assistance Activities
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-11
By Qu Fatong, Liao Yun, Zhou Jie, and Zhang Lei BEIJING, Nov. 11 -- The 24th Chinese Peacekeeping Contingent to the United Nations Interim Force in Lebanon (UNIFIL), jointly with the Chinese Embassy in Lebanon, recently conducted humanitarian assistance activities in Tyre, southern Lebanon. Chinese peacekeepers visited Bazouriye Official Secondary School, the Mosan Center for Special Needs, and the headquarters of the South Litani Sector of the Lebanese Armed Forces, to donate supplies and provide free medical services. Valued at over $34,000, the donated supplies address the needs of vulnerable groups, support education and public livelihoods, and meet the medical service and support needs of the Lebanese Armed Forces units. (Video Editor: Cheng Sihao)

item.title: Xi says a growing China can be partner to help Europe tackle challenges
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-06
Chinese President Xi Jinping meets with Austrian Chancellor Christian Stocker, who is on an official visit to China, at the Great Hall of the People in Beijing, capital of China, Nov. 6, 2026. (Xinhua/Yin Bogu) BEIJING, Nov. 6 (Xinhua) -- A growing and developing China is not the source of Europe's problems, but a partner that can help Europe address its challenges, said Chinese President Xi Jinping during his meeting with Austrian Chancellor Christian Stocker in Beijing on Friday. Xi stressed that China and Europe should focus on areas of cooperation, resolve economic and trade frictions through dialogue and consultation, and achieve win-win results and common development. Noting that this year marks the 55th anniversary of the establishment of diplomatic relations between China and Austria, Xi said trust and friendship are the valuable features of China-Austria relations, transcending differences in social systems, history, culture and development stages. He called on the two sides to consolidate political mutual trust, sustain the positive momentum of high-level exchanges, enhance mutual trust and dispel misgivings through communication, and lay a solid political foundation for future cooperation. Xi said that during the 15th Five-Year Plan (2026-2030) period, China will foster emerging industries, upgrade traditional industries, and further expand opening-up, with a focus on the service sector. China Opportunity 2.0 will bring not only market dividends but also innovation dividends, he noted. China stands ready to work with Austria to expand practical cooperation in emerging fields such as new-energy vehicles, artificial intelligence, digital economy and green development, and foster new engines for economic and trade growth, Xi said. Noting that China-Austria friendship enjoys extensive public support, Xi said the two sides should expand people-to-people and cultural exchanges, facilitate personnel flows, and bring the peoples of the two countries even closer. Stocker said that Austria is committed to fostering its friendly strategic partnership with China, and adheres to the one-China policy. Stocker called on the two countries to build on the long-standing cooperation and mutual trust to comprehensively strengthen cooperation in trade, investment, science and technology, innovation and other fields, boost cultural, tourism and other people-to-people exchanges, and elevate bilateral relations to new heights. He said Austria actively supports the development of EU-China relations and hopes both sides can resolve economic and trade differences through candid dialogue and consultation. Austria is ready to work with China to uphold multilateralism, strengthen multilateral coordination, advance sustainable development, tackle challenges including climate change, and safeguard global prosperity and stability, added Stocker. Chinese President Xi Jinping meets with Austrian Chancellor Christian Stocker, who is on an official visit to China, at the Great Hall of the People in Beijing, capital of China, Nov. 6, 2026. (Xinhua/Li Xiang)

item.title: Reactivating military-industrial complex, Japan poses risks to global peace and stability: Defense Spokesperson
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-06
BEIJING, Nov. 06 -- "Today, Japanese right-wing forces have cast aside the facade of the "exclusively defense-oriented policy" and are reactivating the military-industrial complex, accelerating efforts to put Japanese society on a war footing and militarize the economy," said Senior Colonel Chen Xi, spokesperson for China's defense ministry, at a regular press briefing on Friday. He also added that this poses systemic risks to the safety and well-being of the Japanese people, as well as to global peace and stability. Chen made the remarks while answering media question about Japanese government's plan to include a "virtuous cycle between defense and the economy" as one of the key pillars in its annual revision of the three security documents. He first pointed out that it is a smokescreen used by Japan's ruling authorities to accelerate their drive toward "remilitarization" under the guise of the so-called strategy of "building the country through military-industrial development." Before World War II, Japan's military-industrial complex was deeply embedded in the country's economy, held national decision-making hostage, and underpinned military expansion, becoming a major force driving Japan's aggression abroad. At the end of his remarks, the spokesperson said that the international community must remain highly vigilant and resolutely thwart Japan's attempts to restart its "war machine" and embark once again on the disastrous path of expansionism, jointly safeguarding the postwar international order.
